# p10k-rs v0.2.7

**The "ship a man page" release.** Closes the section-1 man page TODO
that's been carried in the AUR source PKGBUILD since v0.2.0 and wires
it into every install path.

## What's new

### `docs/man/p10k-rs.1`

Standard section-1 man page covering every subcommand:

```sh
man p10k-rs
```

Sections: `NAME`, `SYNOPSIS`, `DESCRIPTION`, `COMMANDS` (all 13),
`FILES`, `ENVIRONMENT`, `PLATFORM NOTES` (the Windows reductions),
`SEE ALSO`, `AUTHOR`, `LICENSE`. Renders zero-warning under
`man --warnings -E UTF-8` (groff on Ubuntu 22.04).

### Distribution chain

| Install path | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Release tarball (unix) | Now contains `man1/p10k-rs.1` next to the binary |
| `install.sh` | Copies to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/man/man1/p10k-rs.1` after the binary install |
| Homebrew formula | `man1.install "man1/p10k-rs.1"` (File.exist? guarded) |
| AUR `p10k-rs-bin` | `/usr/share/man/man1/p10k-rs.1` |
| AUR `p10k-rs` (source) | Already wired since `609a1c6` |
| Windows | Skipped — no native man infrastructure |

`install.sh` prints a `MANPATH` hint when `$XDG_DATA_HOME/man` isn't
already on the resolver path; some BSD man implementations don't pick
it up by default.

## Verification

```sh
# Linux/macOS after install.sh
man p10k-rs

# Direct from the release tarball
tar xzf p10k-rs-0.2.7-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
man -l p10k-rs-0.2.7-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/man1/p10k-rs.1
```

## What's the same

Everything else. The binary itself is byte-identical to v0.2.6 modulo
the Cargo version bump and any rebuild-dependent metadata. Schema,
themes, segments, every gate — unchanged.
